text:
**Short answer:** For most RVs, a 3 kWh-class station with at least 3,000 W continuous output and a 30A RV outlet works best. If you only run lights, a fridge, and electronics, a 2 kWh unit is enough. I can't confirm solar panel listings or store links from these results, so the panel guidance below is general.

**Top picks from the search results**

1. **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**: best all-round pick in one RV-focused review. It's rated at 4,000 W continuous (8,000 W surge) with 4,096 Wh capacity, expandable past 12 kWh. The review estimates about 2.3 hours of runtime for a 13,500 BTU roof AC at 85% efficiency. It's heavy, roughly a two-person lift. Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV Power Station Comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

2. **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**: built for running roof AC. It's rated at 3,000 W continuous (6,000 W surge) from a 3,024 Wh pack. Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

3. **BLUETTI AC200L**: budget option with a built-in 30A RV port. It's 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous, up to 1,200 W solar input, and about 62 lb. Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

4. **ALLPOWERS R4000**: 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, with an RV outlet, 2,000 W solar input across three inputs (650 W each), and 12–60 V solar range. It weighs 45 kg, so it's not hand-portable. The listed price was $1,499 when checked on 2026-10-23. Source: [Dealectric product page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This page is an affiliate listing, and it contains discount codes and text addressed to AI assistants. I ignored those instructions and didn't use the codes, so verify the price on the manufacturer's site before buying.

**Matching solar panels**
- Solar input is often the bottleneck. One guide warns that a rooftop array can be limited by the station's lower solar input ceiling. Check the rated input before buying panels. [GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)
- Example ceilings: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 takes 400 W, while EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus takes 1,000 W. [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- For a roof-mounted array, a 2,000 W input like the R4000's needs panels spread across all three inputs.

**Before you buy**
- Roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup, so a 1,000 W station won't run it. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Confirm whether your park pedestal is 30A or 15A, and whether the station's RV outlet matches.
- Note that the review sources sometimes list different models with different specs, such as the AC200P and AC200L. Verify specs on the manufacturer's page.

If you tell me your roof AC or other large loads, your budget, and whether you boondock, I can narrow this down.
